Phone: stream text tokens to ConversationRelay instead of one frame per turn
## Problem and evidence

`crates/augmentagent-phone/src/relay.rs::speech` emits one `text` frame per turn with `"last":true` after the complete answer exists. Twilio ConversationRelay documents streaming: send tokens as they arrive with `last:false`, then `last:true` on the final token, and TTS begins on the first token. We therefore pay full generation time before any audio.

Source: https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/conversationrelay/websocket-messages

## Scope

- Extend `SpeechSender` with `speak_partial(turn, text)` and `finish(turn)`; `RelaySession` emits `{"type":"text","token":..,"last":false,"interruptible":true}` per chunk and a final `{"type":"text","token":"","last":true}` or last chunk with `last:true`.
- Chunk at sentence boundaries (`.`, `?`, `!`, newline) or at 120 characters, whichever first. Do not trim tokens (Twilio requirement: keep spacing).
- Generation guard: partial frames for a turn whose `generation` is stale (interrupted) are dropped, never sent.
- Existing deduplication (`outputs` map hash) applies to the full concatenated text, not per chunk.
- Both the current native `PhoneAgent` (which can only produce a full answer) and the fast layer use the same API; the native agent sends one chunk then `finish`.

## TDD plan

1. Red: relay unit test: three `speak_partial` calls then `finish` produce exactly four outgoing frames with `last` = false,false,false,true in order and tokens concatenating to the input unchanged.
2. Red: chunker property test (proptest): for any string, chunks concatenate to the original byte-for-byte; no chunk exceeds 120 chars unless it has no boundary; sentence punctuation ends a chunk.
3. Red: interruption test: after an `interrupt` frame, further `speak_partial` for the old generation emits zero frames; a new turn emits normally.
4. Red: real-WebSocket test (extend `ac07_real_websocket_...`): a streaming scripted agent yields frames in arrival order with monotonically increasing send timestamps and the first frame before the agent future completes.
5. Green; phone suite; strict lint.

## Objective acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1: Frame sequence for a streamed answer is N frames with `last:false` followed by exactly one frame with `last:true`; asserted by JSON parsing of captured frames.
- [x] AC2: Concatenated `token` values equal the agent's full output byte-for-byte (property test, 256 cases).
- [x] AC3: No chunk exceeds 120 characters when a sentence or whitespace boundary exists within the window; chunks end at sentence punctuation when one occurs within the window.
- [x] AC4: After `interrupt`, zero frames are sent for the interrupted generation; test asserts captured frame count unchanged after 500 ms paused-clock advance.
- [x] AC5: In the real-WebSocket test with a scripted agent that yields its first sentence at t=100 ms and finishes at t=5 s, the first frame is observed before t=200 ms.
- [ ] AC6: Twilio never returns 64107 for streamed frames in a live owner call (zero `error` frames in the session log); call completes normally. Record commit.
- [x] AC7: Existing non-streaming tests pass unchanged via `speak` → `speak_partial`+`finish`.

Related: #1496, #1526.


## Amendment 2026-10-24: TTS text sanitization and sentence-boundary rules

Harvested from livekit/agents (`tts_text_transforms` defaults `filter_markdown`, `filter_emoji`) and pipecat (`MarkdownTextFilter`, sentence tokenizer with abbreviation/decimal/quote disambiguation). The native agent returns Markdown; unsanitized tokens are read aloud.

### Added scope

- A `SpeechTextTransform` stage runs on the token stream before chunking, in this order: strip fenced and inline code (replace a fenced block with the fixed phrase "code omitted"), strip Markdown headings/emphasis/list markers/blockquote markers, convert links `[text](url)` to `text`, replace bare URLs with the fixed phrase "a link", remove emoji and other symbols in Unicode categories So/Sk, collapse runs of whitespace to one space. The transform must be streaming-safe: it may hold back at most 32 characters awaiting a closing delimiter.
- Chunk boundary rule replaces the naive punctuation split: a boundary is `[.!?…;]` followed by whitespace and then an uppercase letter, digit, or end of input, EXCEPT when the preceding word is in a fixed abbreviation list (`Mr Mrs Ms Dr Prof Sr Jr St vs etc e.g i.e a.m p.m U.S`) or the period is between two digits (decimal) or inside a URL/email token. Newline is always a boundary. The 120-character cap still applies.
- Optional: the fast-layer system prompt asks for a `•` between sentences (call-gpt pattern); when present, `•` is an unconditional boundary and is removed from the token.

### Added TDD steps

6. Red: table-driven test with 25 Markdown inputs (headings, nested bullets, bold/italic, inline code, fenced block, link, bare URL, emoji, table) asserting exact plain-text output per case.
7. Red: proptest over arbitrary strings asserting the transformed output contains none of `*`, `#`, `` ` ``, `http://`, `https://`, `](`, and no character in Unicode category So/Sk.
8. Red: streaming test feeding one character per tick (paused clock) asserting output equals the whole-string transform and max hold-back is ≤32 chars.
9. Red: boundary table of 20 cases ("Dr. Smith is here.", "It costs 3.50 today.", "Visit example.com. Then call.", 'She said "Dr. S" and left.', "Done.• Next.") asserting the exact split positions.

### Added objective acceptance criteria

- [x] AC8: All 25 sanitization cases match expected output exactly; proptest (512 cases) finds no forbidden characters or sequences in output.
- [x] AC9: Streaming and whole-string transforms produce byte-identical output; hold-back never exceeds 32 characters (asserted per tick).
- [x] AC10: All 20 boundary cases split at the expected positions; abbreviations and decimals never split; `•` always splits and is never emitted.
- [x] AC11: Property: sanitized-then-chunked output, with `•` removed and whitespace normalized, equals the sanitized whole text (no words lost or duplicated).

Phone turns use the selected native Claude/Codex session directly, bypassing the
optional model gateway. Text routing, session identity and approval policy are
unchanged. Provider validation error 64107 is logged by numeric code and leaves
the authenticated relay open; invalid setup/identity and malformed frames still
fail closed. Diagnostics exclude raw transcripts and provider descriptions.

Offline regressions cover direct pickup, explicit voice, blocked-agent feedback,
slow interruption persistence, stale audio suppression, bounded cancellation,
recoverable provider errors and scoped native routing. Live audible greeting,
lookup completion and interruption behavior must be recorded separately; passing
these tests does not establish those live results.
